title: Astronomical Distance
body:
Three units, each suited to a different scale, because writing astronomical distances in
kilometres produces numbers nobody can compare.

```
astronomical unit (AU)   the Earth-Sun distance, 1.5 × 10⁸ km      solar system
light-year (ly)          how far light travels in a year,
                         9.5 × 10¹² km  =  63,000 AU               nearby stars
parsec (pc)              3.26 light-years, the distance at which
                         1 AU subtends 1 arcsecond                 professional use
```

The parsec looks arbitrary and is the natural unit for [[Stellar Parallax]], because it
makes the distance formula $d = 1/p$ with no constant attached.

The light-year carries a second meaning beyond distance. Light from an object 1000 light-years
away left 1000 years ago, so every observation is a record of the past and no telescope shows
the universe as it is now. At cosmological distances that becomes the tool, since looking far
enough away means observing the early universe directly.

Scale comparisons worth keeping:

```
Earth to Sun            8 light-minutes
Sun to Proxima          4.25 light-years
across the Milky Way    100,000 light-years
to Andromeda            2.5 million light-years
observable universe     93 billion light-years across
```
